data.generation: exact affine transition of the OU SDE at each integer step (the truth is affine, so exact sampling is available; no EM discretization is used for data generation)
data.initial_law: z_0 ~ N(0, 1) (declared cut: the paper's main text states 8192 samples on t = 0..63 at integer times but does not state the initial law; N(0, 1) is chosen here and recorded)
data.note: Paper Section 4.1: time-dependent Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process dz = (mu*t - theta*z) dt + sigma o dW, mu = 0.02, theta = 0.1, sigma = 0.4, 8192 samples from t = 0 to t = 63 sampled at every integer. Data are regenerated here (the paper does not publish the generated dataset itself). No observation noise is added: the paper samples the SDE itself, not a noisy observation of it.

distillation.library_variables: polynomials in (t, z): the teacher is a time-dependent SDE, so the SINDy library is built on the 2D input (t, z), not on z alone
distillation.oracle_diagnostic: the same SINDy procedure fitted to ground-truth field values at the same query states (diagnostic ceiling only, not a candidate)
distillation.query_states: observed (t, z) pairs of each split (trajectory-disjoint train/validation/test), teacher evaluated directly (no finite differences)
distillation.selection: per field, minimize validation NRMSE against the teacher; test evaluated once after selection

ground_truth_sde.form: dz = (mu*t - theta*z) dt + sigma dW (Stratonovich in the paper; identical to Ito here because sigma is constant)

H1_drift_distillation.note: true drift is degree 1 in (t, z), so the degree-1 validation NRMSE should be within 10% of the best degree's

H3_truth_recovery.coefficient_rule: coefficient thresholds apply ONLY if the pre-registered collinearity diagnostic on train query states gives VIF(t, z) <= 10; if VIF > 10 the verdict rests on the field-level clause alone and coefficients are reported descriptively (Day 1 reflection: separate field-level and coefficient-level hypotheses when collinearity is high)
H3_truth_recovery.sign_match: both true drift monomials (t and z)

H5_estimator_bias.note: Day 1 left constant-diffusion recovery unresolved for the nonlinear Lorenz system (no 1-step estimator recovered g = 0.15 in components 2-3). This linear system tests whether the failure was nonlinearity-driven: the substep estimator should recover sigma = 0.4 better than plain EM

paper.authors: Patrick Kidger, James Foster, Xuechen Li, Terry J. Lyons
paper.code: https://github.com/google-research/torchsde (neural SDE example code referenced by the paper)
paper.experiment: Section 4.1: synthetic example, time-dependent one-dimensional Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process
paper.title: Neural SDEs as Infinite-Dimensional GANs

teacher.architecture: drift MLP and diffusion MLP, each Linear(2,32)-Softplus-Linear(32,32)-Softplus-Linear(32,1) on standardized (t, z) inputs; diffusion output Softplus + 0.01 floor. Smaller than the paper's width-64 nets (CPU cut); the paper additionally applies a final tanh to drift and diffusion, which is NOT used here because it would cap the drift range below the paper's own drift values at large t.
teacher.deviation_from_paper: The paper trains a neural SDE generator against a neural CDE discriminator with a Wasserstein GAN loss, so that the model matches distributions on path space without any density. Reproducing that GAN (neural CDE discriminator, gradient penalty, double backward) is out of CPU scope for one day, and its latent/hidden coordinates are not identifiable for a symbolic equation in any case. This study therefore estimates a neural SDE directly in the observed 1D coordinate, with drift and diffusion as separate MLPs of (t, z), trained by Gaussian transition likelihoods. This is a declared scope cut, not the paper's model: the paper's claim (marginal/path-distribution recovery) is NOT re-tested here; what is tested is the field-level content of such a neural SDE (drift/diffusion as functions of (t, z)) and its polynomial distillability. The paper's SDE is Stratonovich; the likelihoods here use the Ito convention, which coincides with Stratonovich for the constant true diffusion and is diagnosed for the fitted teacher via the 0.5*g*g' correction size.
teacher.estimator: substep_moments (the distilled teacher, chosen A PRIORI per the Day 1 reflection: when the absolute diffusion level is a primary question, use a simulation-based estimator with internal substeps from the start, not a 1-step likelihood)

estimators_compared.em: v1 plain Euler-Maruyama Gaussian transition likelihood: mean z + f*dt, var g^2*dt
estimators_compared.local_linearization: v2 truncated local linearization: mean z + f*dt + 0.5*dt^2*A*f, var g^2*dt + A*g^2*dt^2, A = df/dz (Jacobian treated as a fixed local coefficient, central finite difference, no_grad)
estimators_compared.local_linearization_exp: v3 matrix-exponential resummation with coefficients frozen at the step start: mean z + Psi*f with Psi = (exp(A*dt)-1)/A, var kappa*g^2 with kappa = (exp(2*A*dt)-1)/(2*A)
estimators_compared.substep_moments: v4 simulation-based moment propagation with K = 8 internal substeps per observation interval: per substep, mean advanced by f at the current mean and variance by (2*A*v + g^2)*h, A clamped to [-5, 5] and treated as a fixed local coefficient (central finite difference, no_grad); the Gaussian NLL is evaluated at the observed endpoint under the propagated (mean, variance)

teacher.optimizer: Adam lr 0.003, checkpoint = min validation NLL
